博隆豎琴是源自西非馬里的傳統弦樂器，音色溫潤而富有詩意。其音質兼具明亮與暗沉的特: The bolon is a traditional string instrument from Mali in West Africa, with a warm, poetic timbre. Its tone is both bright and dark: the treble is clear and nimble, the middle and low warm and resonant. It makes sound through the vibration of the strings and has a good range of volume levels. The bolon's range is wide and it can show fine changes of timbre; against the Western harp it has more of a raw, local character but is no less elegant. Its sound carries and spreads naturally through a space. Beside the brightness of the guitar the bolon is deeper; beside the steadiness of the piano it has more nimbleness and intimacy: a timbre both mysterious and familiar.
博隆豎琴為三弦樂器，發聲體為弦，琴身以大型葫芦製成，葫芦表面覆以未剃毛的山羊皮，: The bolon is a three-string instrument whose sounding body is the strings; the body is made from a large gourd covered with unshaved goatskin, and the neck is bow-shaped. The source states the materials only of these parts; the string material, the fittings, the details of the resonator and so on are not described. As a traditional Mande harp of Mali, Gambia and Guinea, its structure is defined mainly by the gourd, the goatskin and the bow-shaped neck.
博隆豎琴為弦鳴樂器，在馬利與幾內亞的傳統場合中，曾用於狩獵儀式或戰前，以激發戰士: The bolon is a chordophone; in traditional settings in Mali and Guinea it was played at hunting rituals or before battle, to stir the courage of the warriors; in Gambia the Jola use it to accompany a male-voice chorus. When listening, note the interweaving of the three plucked strings and the striking of the gourd resonator; the player holds the instrument between the legs with the strings facing him. 博隆豎琴為曼德傳統豎琴，見於馬利、甘比亞與幾內亞。在幾內亞其他弦鳴樂器中，它屬最: The bolon is a harp of the Mande tradition, found in Mali, Gambia and Guinea. Among the other chordophones of Guinea it is the oldest. It is played at hunting rituals and before battle to raise the warriors' courage; in Gambia the Jola also use it to accompany a male-voice chorus. It is a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 323.1.
博隆豎琴（Bolon）是馬利、幾內亞的傳統豎琴，屬弦鳴樂器，H-S 編號 323: The bolon is a traditional harp of Mali and Guinea, a chordophone, H-S 323.1. Its body is a large gourd covered with unshaved goatskin, with a bow-shaped neck and three strings. It is held between the legs with the strings facing the player, and besides plucking, the gourd is struck like a drum. The Jola of Gambia use it to accompany a male-voice chorus; it was also played at hunting rituals and before battle to raise the warriors' courage. Among the other string instruments of Guinea it is the oldest.
坐姿將琴靠於肩上或置於身前。將樂器穩定持於身前。左手負責按弦或改變有效弦長以控制: Sit and rest the harp on your shoulder or hold it in front of you. Hold the instrument steady in front of you. The left hand stops the strings, or changes the sounding length, to control pitch, and the right hand sets the strings vibrating. A chordophone works by the vibration of the string being amplified through a resonating body. Pluck the strings with the fingertips or a plectrum, watching the angle and force of contact.
